sections.overview: Amatitlania coatepeque is a small Central American cichlid described from Lake Coatepeque, a volcanic lake in western El Salvador. Its taxonomic rank is disputed: the current Catalog of Fishes lists it as valid, while a 2014 molecular and morphological study treated the lake population as part of A. nigrofasciata.
sections.identification: It has the short, deep-bodied form and dark vertical bars typical of the convict-cichlid group. The original diagnosis emphasized a possible Y-shaped joining of the fourth and fifth flank bars, but later sampling found that pattern variable and not unique to this population. FishBase reports a maximum standard length of 9.1 cm for a male or unsexed specimen; no comparable female range, body mass, body width or standard height is published in the consulted references. Standard length is measured from the snout to the base of the tail, not to its tip.
sections.habitat: FishBase records it only in Lake Coatepeque, among rocks in clear water and down to 6 m depth.
sections.diet: FishBase contains no diet entry for this species, so its prey and feeding proportions remain undocumented.
sections.behavior: FishBase provides no published field observations of social behavior or daily activity for this population.
sections.reproduction: The FishBase species account lists no breeding season, clutch size or parental-care observations for the Coatepeque fish.
sections.ecology: It occupies a freshwater lake-bottom niche; the Coatepeque population is geographically isolated whether treated as a species or as A. nigrofasciata.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports that the species has not been evaluated on the IUCN Red List. McMahan and colleagues noted substantial shoreline alteration and recommended monitoring the lake’s convict-cichlid population; this is a conservation concern for the isolated population, not evidence of a quantified decline or a formal threatened category.
